question.problem:
Find the solution to the inequality $\frac{5t-6}{2}\le 1.$

The solution is $t$
{{field-1}}{{field-2}}.
question.worked_solution:
First, we clear the rational expression by multiplying both sides by $2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5t-6}{2}\le 1 \\ 2\cdot (\frac{5t-6}{2}) & \le 2\cdot 1 \\ \cancel{2}\cdot (\frac{5t-6}{\cancel{2}}) & \le 2 \\ 5t-6 & \le 2\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we apply the addition and multiplication principles:

$$
\begin{aligned}5t-6 & \le 2 \\ 5t-6+6 & \le 2+6 \\ 5t & \le 8 \\ \frac{5t}{5} & \le \frac{8}{5} \\ t & \le \frac{8}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $t\le \frac{8}{5}.$
